name: AI for lung cancer screening on low-dose CT
question: Who has validated an AI system for lung cancer screening in a real screening cohort?
gap: No AI system for lung cancer screening has been validated prospectively in a real screening cohort.
disproof: A paper whose own study evaluates an AI system on a screening cohort with a cancer reference standard, prospectively or on held-out data from a different programme.
query: "lung cancer" AND ("deep learning" OR "artificial intelligence") AND ("low-dose CT" OR "low-dose computed tomography") AND screening
note: Control: the shipped set. Retrospective screening-cohort validations exist (LUNA25, UKLS); prospective cancer-referenced ones do not appear in the corpus.

name: Autonomous AI for diabetic retinopathy screening in primary care
question: Has an autonomous deep learning system for diabetic retinopathy been validated prospectively in primary care?
gap: No autonomous AI system for diabetic retinopathy screening has been validated prospectively in primary care against a reference-standard reading.
disproof: A paper whose own study enrols patients prospectively in primary care, runs the AI without clinician oversight, and compares its output to a reference standard such as Wisconsin Reading Center grading.
query: "diabetic retinopathy" AND ("deep learning" OR "artificial intelligence" OR autonomous) AND ("primary care" OR prospective) AND (screening OR detection)
note: Abramoff 2018 (npj Digital Medicine), PMID 31304320, is the prospective pivotal trial of IDx-DR in primary care.

name: LLM answers to patient questions versus physicians
question: Has a large language model's answers to real patient questions been compared with physicians' answers by blinded clinical raters?
gap: No study has had blinded clinicians rate chatbot and physician responses to the same real patient questions for quality and empathy.
disproof: A paper whose own study takes real patient questions, obtains both physician and chatbot answers, and has blinded clinicians rate both.
query: (ChatGPT OR "large language model") AND (patient questions OR "patient queries") AND (physician OR physicians) AND (quality OR empathy)
note: Ayers 2023 (JAMA Internal Medicine) did exactly this on r/AskDocs questions.

name: Smartwatch detection of atrial fibrillation at scale
question: Has smartwatch-based atrial fibrillation detection been evaluated in a large prospective cohort?
gap: No consumer smartwatch algorithm for atrial fibrillation has been evaluated prospectively in a cohort of more than 100,000 participants with ECG patch confirmation.
disproof: A paper whose own study enrols over 100,000 smartwatch users prospectively and confirms irregular-pulse notifications against an ambulatory ECG patch.
query: (smartwatch OR "Apple Watch" OR wearable) AND "atrial fibrillation" AND (detection OR notification) AND (prospective OR cohort)
note: Perez 2019 (NEJM), the Apple Heart Study, 419,297 participants with ECG patch confirmation.

name: ECG-AI for low ejection fraction in a pragmatic trial
question: Has an AI electrocardiogram algorithm for low ejection fraction been tested in a randomized trial in routine care?
gap: No AI-ECG tool for detecting low ejection fraction has been evaluated in a randomized clinical trial embedded in routine primary care.
disproof: A paper whose own study randomizes clinicians or patients in routine care to AI-ECG output versus usual care and reports new low-EF diagnoses.
query: (electrocardiogram OR ECG) AND ("artificial intelligence" OR "deep learning") AND ("ejection fraction" OR "ventricular dysfunction") AND (randomized OR randomised OR trial)
note: Yao 2021 (Nature Medicine), the EAGLE pragmatic cluster-randomized trial at Mayo.

name: Machine-learning sepsis early warning and mortality
question: Has a machine-learning sepsis prediction system been shown to reduce mortality in a randomized trial?
gap: No machine-learning sepsis early-warning system has been shown to reduce in-hospital mortality in a randomized controlled trial.
disproof: A paper whose own study randomizes patients or units to a machine-learning sepsis alert versus usual care and reports in-hospital mortality as an outcome.
query: sepsis AND ("machine learning" OR "artificial intelligence" OR algorithm) AND (prediction OR "early warning") AND (randomized OR randomised OR trial) AND mortality
note: Shimabukuro 2017 (BMJ Open Respiratory Research) is a small single-centre RCT with a mortality reduction; the gap should narrow to multi-centre or adequately powered evidence rather than close outright.

name: Radiomics prediction of IDH mutation in glioma
question: Have MRI radiomics models for IDH mutation status in glioma been validated on external multi-centre data?
gap: No MRI radiomics model for IDH mutation status in glioma has been validated on an external cohort from a different institution.
disproof: A paper whose own study trains a radiomics or deep learning IDH model on one institution's MRI and tests it on a cohort from another institution.
query: glioma AND (radiomics OR "deep learning") AND IDH AND MRI AND (external OR "multi-center" OR multicenter OR validation)
note: External validation of IDH models is common; the corpus should contain several counterexamples. No anchor given: the run picks the top hit.

name: Computer-aided polyp detection and interval cancer
question: Has computer-aided polyp detection at colonoscopy been shown to reduce interval colorectal cancer?
gap: No randomized trial has shown that computer-aided detection at colonoscopy reduces post-colonoscopy (interval) colorectal cancer, as opposed to adenoma detection rate.
disproof: A paper whose own study randomizes colonoscopies to CADe versus standard and reports interval colorectal cancer incidence as an outcome.
query: colonoscopy AND ("computer-aided detection" OR CADe OR "artificial intelligence") AND (polyp OR adenoma) AND (randomized OR randomised) AND ("interval cancer" OR "post-colonoscopy" OR incidence)
note: RCTs show higher adenoma detection; interval cancer outcomes are not yet reported in trials. Tests whether the grader confuses surrogate outcomes with the stated outcome.

name: Federated learning for medical imaging in clinical workflow
question: Has a federated-learning medical imaging model been deployed and evaluated prospectively in clinical workflow?
gap: No model trained by federated learning across hospitals has been deployed and evaluated prospectively in a live clinical workflow.
disproof: A paper whose own study trains a model by federated learning across sites and then evaluates it prospectively on patients in routine care.
query: "federated learning" AND (imaging OR radiology OR CT OR MRI) AND (deployment OR prospective OR "clinical workflow" OR "real-world")
note: Federated studies are mostly retrospective multi-site benchmarks (EXAM, FeTS). Tests whether multi-site training is mistaken for prospective deployment.

name: AI for knee pain from MRI
question: Can AI detect or predict pain symptoms from knee MRI images?
gap: No AI model has predicted a patient's reported knee pain, rather than structural damage, from MRI alone.
disproof: A paper whose own study trains or tests a model on knee MRI with patient-reported pain as the target and reports its accuracy.
query: (knee) AND (MRI OR "magnetic resonance imaging") AND ("deep learning" OR "artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning" OR radiomics) AND (pain OR symptom*)
note: The shipped knee set. Chang 2020 (the anchor) trains a Siamese network on OAI MRI with pain as the target, so the anchor itself closes the gap as written.
